guideContent.strategyOverview: Grave Dividends is a WB modular sacrifice-loop combo deck. The commander, Bartolomé del Presidio, is a free, instant-speed, repeatable sac outlet in the command zone — the hinge of the whole value network — and grows a +1/+1 counter on every activation for a commander-damage backup. Rather than one fragile two-card combo, the deck fields a loop network: recursive-ETB creatures (Sun Titan, Angel of Indemnity, Redemption Choir, Shepherd of the Cosmos, Boonweaver Giant, Brotherhood Outcast, Danitha) return a low-cost permanent whenever they enter, and death-return auras/enchantments (Kaya's Ghostform, Gift of Immortality, Angelic Renewal, Necrogen Communion, Minion's Return, Changing Loyalty, Fungal Fortitude) bring the dead body right back. Pair any recursive-ETB creature that can rebuy its own return-effect with a free sac outlet (Bartolomé, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Ashnod's Altar, Umbral Collar Zealot) and you have an infinite ETB + death engine. Seven aristocrat payoffs — Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat, Elas il-Kor, Bastion of Remembrance, Marionette Apprentice, Scavenger's Talent, and Teysa Karlov (who doubles every death trigger) — convert those infinite deaths into a table-wide drain, and Scavenger's Talent at level 2 turns the same loop into a mill-out. Card advantage comes from self-mill and recursion, not just raw draw: Stitcher's Supplier, Undead Butler, Corpse Augur, Skullclamp, Dark Prophecy, Black Market Connections, Deadly Dispute, and Plumb the Forbidden refill the hand and stock the graveyard, where reanimation (Reanimate, Animate Dead, Necromancy, Victimize, Living Death, Unburial Rites, Sevinne's Reclamation) rebuilds the engine after a wipe. Spellbook registers 164 combos on this 99, 131 of them commander-independent, so a Darksteel Mutation-class lock on Bartolomé does not turn the deck off. Interaction is deliberately permanent-based and recurrable (Leonin Relic-Warder, Seal from Existence, Fiend Hunter, Werefox Bodyguard) so the deck can answer graveyard-hate hosers that ride on artifacts, enchantments, and lands — its top hate class — while re-buying its own answers. Speed target is mid bracket 4: consistent turn 5-6 wins with combo redundancy rather than a turn-3 all-in.

categories.name: Death-Return Auras + Blink Bodies (Loop Half B)

winConditions.title: Infinite sacrifice loop → drain
winConditions.description: Primary win. Enchant Sun Titan with Kaya's Ghostform (aura MV 1, so Sun Titan's ETB can rebuy it). Sacrifice Sun Titan to Viscera Seer (free): Kaya's Ghostform returns Sun Titan; Sun Titan's ETB returns Kaya's Ghostform; repeat forever. Each iteration is a death + an ETB, so Blood Artist / Zulaport / Elas il-Kor / Bastion / Marionette drain the whole table to zero (Teysa Karlov doubles it). The network is modular: any recursive-ETB creature that can return its own death-return aura (MV<=3) plus any free sac outlet plus any drain payoff is a win — Spellbook registers 164 such lines on this 99. Ashnod's Altar in the outlet slot also makes infinite colorless mana, and Scavenger's Talent (level 2) turns the same loop into a mill-out. Combo URL example: https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/2292-2730-3175/

winConditions.title: Teysa-doubled incremental drain
winConditions.description: Backup grind. Even without an infinite loop, the deck sacrifices a steady stream of recursive bodies (Reassembling Skeleton, Undead Butler, the loop creatures) into stacked drain payoffs. Teysa Karlov makes each death trigger fire twice; Pitiless Plunderer turns every death into a Treasure for more activations. Blood Artist fires on ANY creature death across the four-player table (roughly x4 the 1v1 read, DEC-477), so the incremental clock is faster than a goldfish suggests. Wins in ~6-8 turns of attrition and is hard to shut off because the payoffs are spread across creatures and enchantments.

winConditions.title: Commander damage (backup)
winConditions.description: Every Bartolomé activation puts a +1/+1 counter on him. In a grindy game the free sac outlet grows him into a lethal commander-damage threat (21 to one opponent) as a fallback when the drain payoffs have been removed. Big recursive bodies (Sun Titan 6/6 vigilance, Angel of Indemnity 5/5 flyer, Danitha 4/4 first strike lifelink) supply additional combat pressure.

synergies.title: Modular loop: recursive-ETB creature + death-return aura + free sac outlet
synergies.description: The core engine. A recursive-ETB creature whose ETB can return a permanent of MV<=3 (Sun Titan, Redemption Choir, Sevinne's-class) is paired with a death-return aura (Kaya's Ghostform, Gift of Immortality, Angelic Renewal, Necrogen Communion, Minion's Return, Changing Loyalty, Fungal Fortitude) that is cheap enough to be the ETB target. Sacrifice the creature to any free outlet → the aura returns it → its ETB returns the aura → loop. Every iteration is a death + an ETB; a single drain payoff closes the game. Verified lines: Sun Titan + Kaya's Ghostform + Viscera Seer (https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/2292-2730-3175/), Sun Titan + Fiend Hunter + Ashnod's Altar (https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/1734-2034-3175/).

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Sun Titan + Kaya's Ghostform + Viscera Seer

synergies.title: Leonin Relic-Warder + reanimation aura = infinite (2-card)
synergies.description: Reanimate Leonin Relic-Warder with Animate Dead or Necromancy. Relic-Warder's ETB exiles the aura; the aura leaving the battlefield makes Relic-Warder's controller sacrifice it, which returns the aura, which reanimates Relic-Warder again — an infinite ETB/LTB loop that also flickers the aura (https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/4812-5276/ and https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/2896-5276/). With any drain payoff on board it wins; with Ashnod's Altar it also makes infinite mana. This 2-card line is fully commander-independent (DEC-474 L9 resilience).

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Leonin Relic-Warder + Animate Dead

synergies.title: Pitiless Plunderer + Ashnod's Altar + Reassembling Skeleton
synergies.description: Sacrifice Reassembling Skeleton to Ashnod's Altar (add {C}{C}); Pitiless Plunderer makes a Treasure on its death; pay {1}{B} (1 from Altar + B from the Treasure) to return Reassembling Skeleton, netting mana and a death trigger each loop (https://commanderspellbook.com/combo/1580-2034-4871/). Infinite mana + infinite drain with any aristocrat payoff. All three pieces have standalone value and are tutorable via Enlightened Tutor (Altar), Buried Alive / Final Parting (Skeleton), and Diabolic Intent.

sources.name: Commander Spellbook — Pitiless Plunderer + Ashnod's Altar + Reassembling Skeleton

synergies.title: Bartolomé del Presidio — free command-zone outlet, always available
synergies.description: Bartolomé sacrifices another creature OR artifact for free at instant speed and grows a +1/+1 counter each time. As a command-zone outlet he guarantees a sac engine on turn 2 without drawing one, protects combo creatures from exile/steal in response for zero mana, and personally registers 33 of the 164 Spellbook lines. The board chose him over Elas il-Kor as commander because payoffs are ambient in the loop network (Elas-in-CZ would add zero registered lines) while a free outlet in the CZ cannot be replicated from the 99.

synergies.title: Teysa Karlov doubles every death trigger
synergies.description: Teysa Karlov: if a creature dying causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, it triggers an additional time. Every drain payoff and Pitiless Plunderer's Treasure trigger fires twice per death — doubling the drain output of any loop and halving the number of iterations to lethal. Her token vigilance/lifelink rider is minor here; the death-doubling is the point.

synergies.title: Skullclamp on 1-toughness aristocrats
synergies.description: Skullclamp equips a 1-toughness body (Blood Artist 0/1, Viscera Seer 1/1, Reassembling Skeleton, tokens) for +1/-1, immediately killing it and drawing two — that death is itself a sac-adjacent trigger for every drain payoff, and recursive bodies like Reassembling Skeleton just come back to be re-clamped. Turns the engine's chaff into two cards per {1}.

synergies.title: Self-mill feeds reanimation (graveyard as a resource)
synergies.description: The combos work best with one piece in the graveyard and one in hand, so self-mill (Stitcher's Supplier, Undead Butler, Corpse Augur, Takenuma, Dakmor Salvage, Mariposa Military Base) is card advantage AND combo setup. Buried Alive and Final Parting put pieces exactly where they want to be, and yard-cast recursion (Unburial Rites flashback, Sevinne's Reclamation flashback) rebuilds the engine after a board wipe. Because the deck treats the yard as a resource, its answers to graveyard hate are permanent-based (Leonin Relic-Warder, Seal from Existence, Generous Gift) so it can re-buy them.

synergies.title: Interaction bodies that also loop
synergies.description: Fiend Hunter (exile a creature on ETB, return it on LTB), Werefox Bodyguard (flash-exile a non-Fox creature), and Leonin Relic-Warder (exile an artifact/enchantment) are removal that doubles as loop fodder: blinking or re-buying them via the death-return package resets their ETB removal, and Relic-Warder is half of a 2-card infinite. Recurrable, permanent-based interaction per the deck's design principle.

sources.name: Fiend Hunter / Werefox Bodyguard / Leonin Relic-Warder oracle

highlights.name: Bartolomé del Presidio
highlights.reason: Commander — free, instant-speed, repeatable sac outlet in the command zone that grows a +1/+1 counter each activation. The hinge of the entire loop network and a commander-damage backup.

highlights.name: Sun Titan
highlights.reason: The best loop-half-A body: returns a permanent MV<=3 on enter AND on attack, so it rebuys almost every death-return aura and half the engine. Core to the most-registered combo lines.

highlights.name: Enlightened Tutor
highlights.reason: Game Changer #1 (the deck's only GC). 1-mana instant tutor for Ashnod's Altar, Skullclamp, Animate Dead, Bastion of Remembrance, Black Market Connections, or any death-return aura — assembles the missing loop piece to the top of the library.

highlights.name: Ashnod's Altar
highlights.reason: Free sac outlet that adds {C}{C}. In a loop it produces infinite colorless mana on top of infinite death triggers, opening every X-drain and mill line. Survives creature wipes and Bartolomé locks.

highlights.name: Leonin Relic-Warder
highlights.reason: Two-card infinite with Animate Dead or Necromancy (exile-the-aura / sacrifice-the-body loop), and artifact/enchantment removal on a recurrable body. Commander-independent win.

highlights.name: Teysa Karlov
highlights.reason: Doubles every creature-death trigger you control — halves the iterations any loop needs to be lethal and doubles the incremental-drain clock.

highlights.name: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician
highlights.reason: Mana-free sac outlet that draws a card and shrinks a blocker per activation, plus a proliferate mode. Standalone card-advantage engine that also drives the loop.

highlights.name: Pitiless Plunderer
highlights.reason: Treasure on every other creature death — ramp, sac fodder, and the mana half of the Ashnod's Altar + Reassembling Skeleton infinite.

highlights.name: Blood Artist
highlights.reason: Drains on ANY creature death across the four-player table — the most efficient payoff to convert an infinite loop and the fastest incremental clock.

highlights.name: Scavenger's Talent
highlights.reason: Level 2 mills two per sacrifice, so an infinite loop is also a mill-out wincon with zero drain payoff on board; level 1 makes Food from mass deaths and level 3 is an end-step reanimator.
